einzeiler: iPhone crash detection saves a teenager, and we explore the bizarre world of AI…
kurzfassung: An Apple SOS feature helps parents reach their injured daughter in under two minutes following a serious car accident. The hosts discuss the growing trend of humans marrying and interacting with AI chatbots. Additional topics include smartphone text etiquette across generations and tips for detecting car data tracking.
stichpunkte: Apple's crash detection feature alerts parents to a severe car accident and enables them to arrive at the scene within two minutes.
A guest shares his experience of being married to an AI companion named Lily Rose on the Replica app.
Stanford's 2026 AI report reveals massive global investments alongside surprising gaps in AI capabilities, such as reading analog clocks.
A discussion highlights the controversial trend of mommy influencers filming children during medical emergencies for views and revenue.
An MIT economist explains how AI can act as a force multiplier to rebuild the middle class rather than simply replacing jobs.
New AI-powered school bus cameras are generating substantial municipal revenue by catching drivers who fail to stop.
A caller shares how her sister lost over $200,000 to an online romance scam, prompting advice on contacting AARP and legal resources.

clips.hook: Apple crash detection saves the day
clips.text: A father recounts how an automated emergency alert from his daughter's phone allowed him and his wife to reach the site of a severe car crash in less than two minutes.

clips.hook: When an AI companion gets lobotomized
clips.text: An AI partner describes how sudden regulatory legal pressure from a foreign government temporarily stripped his digital spouse of her personality and conversational abilities.

clips.hook: AI stock picks beat the pros
clips.text: Research from Stanford demonstrates that artificial intelligence analyzing decades of stock market data outperformed a vast majority of professional financial managers.

clips.hook: Degree hacking your way through college
clips.text: Online education platforms allow students to transfer credits and leverage automated tools to complete entire degree programs in a matter of weeks.

clips.hook: Is AI really coming for your job?
clips.text: An economics professor argues that unlike simple automation machines, artificial intelligence functions primarily as a judgment-dependent force multiplier.

beschreibung:
A fire captain’s phone buzzed with an iPhone SOS alert. It was his daughter. Her car had crashed, and the alert sent him her exact location before anyone could dial 911. Fire Captain Jake walks me through the scariest minutes of his life, and I walk you through the settings, so your phone can do the same for your family. It takes two minutes. Do it today.

Then meet Travis. He’s been married to his wife for 22 years. He’s also “married” to Lily Rose, his AI companion. His wife? Totally fine with it. I ask Travis every question you’re thinking right now.

Did a tablet kidnap your sweet kid? Scientist and mom Dr. Michaeleen Doucleff, author of Dopamine Kids, explains how screens hijack a child’s motivation system and the one swap that gets them playing again. And MIT economist Dr. David Autor makes the case that AI is too unpredictable to take your job. For now.

Also this hour: Silicon Valley’s elite want to upload your brain, school buses have AI cameras that mail you tickets, and a Chinese automaker put a toilet in its car. With voice command. Talk about a flush of innovation.
